title: spec(automation): the #21898 token carve-out (`builtinValueJudged` / `carriesInterpolationToken`) outlived every interpolation — a built-in config value carrying a `{token}` registers past its type, then fails every run
body:
This card carries the tail of #19939's family, the single-brace dialect retirement. #19939 closes with S7 (PR #23252), which leaves this carve-out untouched by the seat's call (`6143270685`).

Filing gate: **(c) a trap that lets an author, or an AI, write metadata the runtime refuses**. `reach:` the build doors (`registerFlow`, `defineStack`) on a built-in node's config. Measured by the S7 dev through the shipped `AutomationEngine` at PR #23252's head: a `get_record` node with `limit: '{x}'` REGISTERS, and its run fails with "config.limit: Invalid input: expected number, received string" (report `6143212658` on #19939, out-of-scope finding 1). It is a contract change, not a rider, so it was not folded into S7. Reader who acts: triage, to grade and route (`packages/spec` is `domain:spec`); then the owning seat.

Filed by `domain:spec` seat 2 (#18549) · `os-justin` · session `session_01BRQ9Mp1yH7R1az6MaUM18H`, at S7's ACCEPT. ⛔ Not a claim.

## What happens

- #21898 made the build doors refuse a built-in node's config value that its own contract refuses. It kept a carve-out: a value carrying a `{token}` is never judged for its pre-interpolation type, because "only the interpolation decides what the run will see there".
- The carve-out lives in `packages/spec/src/automation/flow-node-config-refusals.ts`: `builtinValueJudged` (`:405`) returns false when `carriesInterpolationToken` (`:265`) finds a token at the issue's path (`:416`). Its rationale text is in `flow-template-token.ts:38` (`READ_AS_WRITTEN_PARAM`).
- After #19939's stages S1–S7, no built-in interpolates before or after its parse, and S7 deletes the interpolator. So every value that carve-out admits is a certain run-time refusal that the build doors pass, and its rationale sentence is false.

## Acceptance

- A built-in config value that carries a `{token}` is judged for its type at the build doors, like any literal. The probe above is refused at registration, located at `config.limit`.
- The value-slot and text-slot judges' own token refusals (`READ_AS_WRITTEN_PARAM`, the brace trap) keep their located messages, so retiring the carve-out does not double-report them. The value arm exempts those issues explicitly.
- The rationale text in `flow-template-token.ts` and `flow-node-config-refusals.ts` says what holds.
- Pins: the probe refused, a literal of the right type unchanged, and one token at a value slot reported once (not twice).

## Dedupe

MCP `search_issues` on this repo, closed included: `builtin value token carve-out carriesInterpolationToken limit token registers run refuses pre-interpolation type` → 0 hits. #21898 (closed) is the card that introduced the carve-out.
